session.question: How many respondents were used for recycling in the 206 survey, and what did the extended VBN theory explain best?
session.answer: The recycling survey used 206 respondents. The extended value-belief-norm (VBN) theory explained sustainable purchase behavior best, relative to household energy and water use, mobility, and recycling. (onel2023transformingconsumptionthe chunk 1)
session.raw_answer: The recycling survey used 206 respondents. The extended value-belief-norm (VBN) theory explained sustainable purchase behavior best, relative to household energy and water use, mobility, and recycling. (pqac-53fa3629)
session.context:
pqac-53fa3629: The study used separate SEMs for four behaviors with different respondent groups: 281 for purchase, 265 for household energy and water use, 273 for mobility, and 206 for recycling. The abstract says the extended value-belief-norm (VBN) theory provided the best explanation for sustainable purchase behaviors, compared with household energy/water use, mobility, and recycling. It also notes the strongest predictors included biospheric values, ecological worldview, personal norms, behavioral intention, awareness of consequences, ascription of responsibility, and low egoistic values for eco-friendly purchases.
From Naz Onel. Transforming consumption: the role of values, beliefs, and norms in promoting four types of sustainable behavior. Journal of Consumer Behaviour, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1002/cb.2212, doi:10.1002/cb.2212.

pqac-afa79249: The excerpt describes a 2023 study that used an extended value-belief-norm (VBN) framework with environmental awareness to explain Chinese university students’ environmentally sustainable behavior as tourists. It reports data from 301 university students in eastern China. The empirical results show environmental awareness positively influences biospheric, altruistic, and egoistic values; biospheric value predicts the New Ecological Paradigm (NEP); and NEP, awareness of consequences, and personal norms mediate the effects. The study concludes that the extended VBN can explain students’ environmentally sustainable behavior and support sustainable tourism.
From Zhihui Wang, Liangzhen Nie, Eila Jeronen, Lihua Xu, and Meiai Chen. Understanding the environmentally sustainable behavior of chinese university students as tourists: an integrative framework. International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph20043317, doi:10.3390/ijerph20043317.

pqac-bab9cfa4: The excerpt is about a 2022 paper testing the Value-Belief-Norm (VBN) theory for willingness to consume circular apparel in Brazil and the Netherlands. It reports that the VBN variables overall explain circular behaviour in the apparel industry and that the model’s paths were supported. It also says VBN predicted willingness to consume circular apparel better in the Netherlands than in Brazil. The excerpt does not mention a 206-respondent survey or specify what the extended VBN theory explained best beyond circular apparel behaviour / willingness to consume circular clothing.
From Giovana Monteiro Gomes, Natália Guimarães Moreira, Thijs Bouman, Aldo Roberto Ometto, and Ellen van der Werff. Towards circular economy for more sustainable apparel consumption: testing the value-belief-norm theory in brazil and in the netherlands. Sustainability, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su14020618, doi:10.3390/su14020618.
